hero.headline: Scripture that takes you seriously.
hero.subhead: A literary Bible translation for those who refuse to choose between intellectual honesty and living faith.

manifesto.p1: Somewhere along the way, we were told to choose: study the Bible critically and risk losing the sacred, or hold onto faith and stop asking hard questions.
manifesto.p2: We don't believe that's the only way.
manifesto.p3: Aperto is a literary translation—poetry as poetry, prose as prose—with ancient context woven directly into the text, clearly marked so you always know what was written and what it meant.
manifesto.p4: It's built on ecumenical scholarship from Catholic, Protestant, Orthodox, and Pentecostal traditions.
manifesto.p5: And it's designed for real encounter—through audio, music, and meditation shaped by how people actually read and grow today.
manifesto.p9: For the curious and the seeking. For those who left and those who stayed. For anyone ready to look again.

falseChoice.title: The False Choice
falseChoice.p1: For a long time, Christianity has felt like it's splitting into two camps.
falseChoice.p2: One takes the text seriously—historically, critically, honestly. It asks hard questions about authorship, context, transmission. It refuses easy answers. But somewhere along the way, it often loses the expectation that Scripture might actually do something to you. Study becomes analysis. The text becomes an artifact.
falseChoice.p3: The other promises encounter, transformation, a living word. It expects God to show up. But it sometimes asks you to stop asking questions—or at least to feel guilty about them. Certainty becomes the measure of faith. Curiosity feels like betrayal.
falseChoice.p4: We think that's a false choice.
falseChoice.p5: The scholars who first studied these texts were monks in prayer. The mystics who encountered God in them were rigorous readers. For most of Christian history, depth of study and depth of encounter weren't opposites—they were the same path.

literary.title: A literary translation
literary.desc: that honors the original forms—poetry as poetry, narrative as narrative, letter as letter. Scripture is literature before it's anything else, and we translate it that way.

context.title: Context made visible
context.desc: The first readers of these texts understood things we don't—cultural assumptions, geographic references, religious background, literary echoes. We weave that context directly into the text, clearly formatted so you always know what was written and what it meant. No more flipping to footnotes to understand why something matters.

ecumenical.title: Ecumenical foundations
ecumenical.desc: Our exegesis draws on Catholic, Protestant, Orthodox, and Pentecostal scholarship. Not to flatten differences, but because the text belongs to the whole Church, and every tradition sees something the others might miss.

multimedia.title: Multimedia encounter
multimedia.desc: Audio Bible. Podcasts that unpack each passage. Original songs that capture the emotional weight of the text. Meditations and devotions. Scripture isn't just read—it's heard, sung, sat with, lived.

design.title: Designed for how people actually engage
design.desc: Informed by research on digital reading and spiritual formation, we build formats that work with attention, not against it—and that support genuine growth, not just information transfer.

europe.title: Scripture for Europe
europe.desc: Available in 11 languages and growing—bringing resources to communities that have waited too long for translations that are both serious and alive.

ai.title: Made possible by AI
ai.desc: Thoughtful workflows let us achieve depth and scale that would otherwise take generations. What once seemed impossible for smaller language communities is now within reach.

audience.believer: For the believer who still thinks.
audience.left: For those who left the church but couldn't leave the questions.
audience.stayed: For those who stayed but feel the tension.
audience.curious: For the spiritually curious and the intellectually honest.
audience.closing: You don't have to have it figured out. You just have to be willing to look.

europe.title: A European Project
europe.p1: Christianity in Europe sits at a crossroads. Historic churches face decline. Evangelical communities remain small. Secular culture has often written off faith as intellectually untenable—and too many expressions of Christianity have confirmed that suspicion.
europe.p2: But there's also hunger. People searching for meaning, for depth, for something that can hold the weight of real life. People who might be open to the Christian story if someone offered it without asking them to stop thinking.
europe.p3: Aperto is built for that moment. A Bible that urban, educated, questioning Europeans can engage without embarrassment—and that might just change them.
europe.p4: We're starting with 11 languages. We won't stop there.

overview.title: Overview
overview.p1: Aperto uses an AI-assisted approach to Bible translation—not to replace human judgement, but to amplify it. We believe combining cutting-edge technology with human insight can help make Scripture accessible to new audiences.
overview.p2: Every translation decision goes through multiple layers of review, combining AI drafts with human expertise, community feedback, and ongoing revision.

theological.title: A Theological Justification
theological.p1: When Jesus said 'I tell you, if these were silent, the very stones would cry out' (Luke 19:40), he was responding to religious leaders who wanted to silence the proclamation of who he was. His point: if the expected voices fall silent, God will use unexpected means.
theological.p2: We don't claim AI is literally the 'stones crying out'. But we do believe that when traditional gatekeepers can't or won't make Scripture accessible to everyone, God's message will find other ways through.
theological.p3: There's a certain poetry to it: silicon chips are, after all, rocks we taught to think. Sand refined, etched with circuits, trained on humanity's collected wisdom. If God can speak through a burning bush, a donkey, or bread and wine—perhaps silicon isn't so strange a medium.
theological.poetry: Silicon chips are rocks we taught to think. Sand refined, etched with circuits, trained on humanity's collected wisdom.
theological.p4: The printing press was once viewed with suspicion by religious authorities. So was translating the Bible into vernacular languages. Every technological shift that democratised access to Scripture was initially resisted—and eventually embraced.

step1.title: Deep Exegesis
step1.desc: Comprehensive scholarly research: Greek text analysis, major commentaries, lexicons, cultural studies, and patristic sources.

step2.title: Translation Draft
step2.desc: AI-assisted draft generation, filtered through our translation philosophy: accessible, literary, honest.

step3.title: Human Review
step3.desc: Translation teams review and refine, ensuring accuracy, literary quality, and faithfulness to the original text.

step4.title: Community Feedback
step4.desc: Open for community input and discussion. Translation improves through conversation.

step5.title: Multimedia Production
step5.desc: Audio Bible, podcasts, songs, and meditations that help the text come alive.
